::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

:::{#exm-not-local-minimizer}
#### A point that is not a local minimizer

For $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$, the point $x = -1$ is not a local minimizer.
For any $t$,

$$
\ba
f(-1 + t)
&= (-1 + t)^3 - 3(-1 + t)
&& \text{(substitute)}
\\
&= (-1 + 3t - 3t^2 + t^3) - 3(-1 + t)
&& \text{(expand the cube)}
\\
&= -1 + 3t - 3t^2 + t^3 + 3 - 3t
&& \text{(multiply } -3 \text{ into the parentheses)}
\\
&= 2 - 3t^2 + t^3
&& \text{(} 3t - 3t = 0 \text{ and } -1 + 3 = 2 \text{)}
\\
&= 2 + t^2 (t - 3)
&& \text{(factor out } t^2 \text{)}
\\
&= f(-1) + t^2 (t - 3),
&& \text{(} f(-1) = (-1)^3 - 3(-1) \text{, which equals } 2 \text{)}
\ea
$$

and $t^2 (t - 3) < 0$ whenever $t \ne 0$ and $t < 3$.
So whatever $\tolin > 0$ is,
the point $x = -1 + t$ with $t = \min\cb{\tolin / 2, 1}$ satisfies $\abs{x - (-1)} < \tolin$
and $f(x) < f(-1)$.
For example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(-0.9) &= -0.729 + 2.7 \\
&= 1.971 \\
&< 2.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
